scope: Final read-only source and current documentation review after pre-await profile snapshot repair

verification.fullApplication: Owned by root; not rerun or inferred from the focused suite

resolvedFindings.issue: Shared read-time strict profile validation would prevent ordinary opening of future or malformed profiles
resolvedFindings.finalState: Existing manifest readers and native opening/seed/archive paths retain the profile data. The planner gives local diagnostics; strict validation belongs to new profile adoption and native template creation.

resolvedFindings.issue: A caller could mutate the newly supplied profile after validation during asynchronous definition locking or template reads
resolvedFindings.finalState: applyProjectDefinition captures profileInput and receives the detached validated studioProfile before the first asynchronous lock; journal and manifest use that snapshot. The regression deliberately mutates original data and replaces definition.studioProfile, and final saved data stays validated.

factChecks.claim: Module declarations describe registered implementation surfaces
factChecks.detail: The seven builtins expose 22 contributions, with version-1 dependency and provider checks. Host flags are separate and do not establish executable installation or tool identity.

factChecks.claim: Future 3D and author Rust behavior remain unavailable
factChecks.detail: No builtin registers scene.representation.scene3d or behavior.rust. Missing and version-incompatible requests report local diagnostics; no template/document type name invokes a Scene2D conversion.

factChecks.claim: The document authority survives system composition
factChecks.detail: The runtime retains source, history, dirty state and ordinary Save. The private composition root injects separate area ports, returns detached metadata, and never exposes controllers or save callbacks.

factChecks.claim: Project declarations are additive and migratable
factChecks.detail: Absent old profiles do not gain requests; omission preserves an existing profile. New profile data is strict and immutable before await. Native optional serialization preserves absent builtin provenance; existing and future declarations survive storage and archive migration.

factChecks.claim: Current docs do not claim complete decomposition
factChecks.detail: STUDIO_MODULES explicitly retains the document lifecycle, World aggregation, build preview/execution aggregation, DOM/HTTP adapters and boot-only lifecycle. STATUS/ARCHITECTURE/ROADMAP keep these distinctions and unpublished scope.

factChecks.claim: The registry is not a plugin permission surface
factChecks.detail: Only exact bounded plain data enters descriptors and requests; accessors, serialization hooks, functions, sparse arrays, inherited custom prototypes and cycles fail admission. There is no code loader, package installation, hot unload, sandbox or authority grant.

factChecks.claim: The build and static scene preview remain partly coupled
factChecks.detail: Composition root forwards independently observed host flags, but the existing build controller still requires its build availability when enabling its scene preview. The new document states this current limitation.

remainingBoundaries: The main document lifecycle is not yet extracted from app-runtime.
World query and mutation views still aggregate inside the existing controller.
Scene authoring, backend projects and runtime work still aggregate within the build surface.
Views still use existing DOM/HTTP/platform imports; per-domain ports do not imply complete transport inversion.
Snapshot diagnostics have no new interactive module configuration or missing-capability panel.
No 3D author format, author Rust compiler, Nuis/native provider or replacement ns-nova GUI is delivered.
No dynamic third-party installation, executable plugin authority, hot reload/unload or automatic migration is delivered.
No installed desktop/Android device acceptance or engine tool installation is inferred from module/host flags or focused tests.
previousReport: core-boundary-review.json retained with its original earlier source identities
